assessment: This elegant study furthers our understanding about the mechanisms by which distributed systems control rhythmic movements of different speeds. The authors trained an artificial recurrent neural network to produce muscle activity patterns similar to those that monkeys generate when performing an arm cycling task at different speeds. The dominant patterns in the neural network do not directly reflect muscle activity, and these dominant patterns do a better job than muscle activity at capturing key features of neural activity recorded from the monkey motor cortex in the same task. In addition to the main result, the study provides a particularly clear example of how thinking in terms of network dynamics can naturally explain empirical observations in terms of the computation being performed.
